methods.ss_score: MaxEntScan maximum-entropy splice-site models (Yeo & Burge 2004, yeo2004), computed with the maxentpy implementation v0.0.4 (maxentpy), which ships the original matrices. score5 on the 9-mer -3..+6 around the donor (3 exonic + 6 intronic nt, GT at +1+2); score3 on the 23-mer -20..+3 around the acceptor (20 intronic + 3 exonic nt, AG at -2-1). Units: bits (log2 odds vs a 1st-order background), higher = stronger; typical real sites ~0-12 (5') and ~0-14 (3'). Validation: maxentpy reproduces the documented reference examples exactly - score5('cagGTAAGT') = 10.858313101356437 and score3('ttccaaacgaacttttgtAGgga') = 2.8867730651152104 (maxentpy README, https://github.com/kepbod/maxentpy); the Burge-lab web server (hollywood.mit.edu/burgelab/maxent) was unreachable from this machine, so the reference values are the implementation's published examples rather than a fresh run of the original Perl. Sites whose window runs off the fetched region, or contains a non-ACGT base, get score null. Branch points are not scored (bp.pos/bp.score always null).
methods.psi: Measured PSI comes from the ASCOT GTEx cassette-exon table (ling2020; snaptron.cs.jhu.edu/data/ascot/gtex_psi.csv.gz), joined to our exons by exact GRCh38 coordinate (chrN:start-end, 1-based inclusive) and gene symbol; ASCOT percentages are divided by 100 so value is a fraction 0-1, and -1 (not measured) is dropped. ASCOT's PSI file carries no per-tissue sample count, so n is null (counts are in ASCOT_accession_metadata.xlsx, not parsed here). VastDB (tapial2017) PSI averages are whole-compendium averages, not one tissue, and are recorded with tissue 'VastDB human compendium (average)' and n null. Alternative-first-exon / alternative-promoter events (CDKN2A, TP63, TP53 delta133, MDM2 P1/P2) are not cassette exons and are in neither table: their psi and isoform_fraction are null, not estimated. No value here is computed or inferred by us.
methods.exon_type: Exon types are derived by comparing the transcripts shipped for that gene (not a curated annotation): 'first'/'last' = the 5'-most / 3'-most exon of at least one transcript; 'alt5' = shares its 5' boundary with another exon that has a different 3' (donor) boundary; 'alt3' = shares its 3' boundary with another exon that has a different 5' (acceptor) boundary; 'cassette' = internal exon absent from at least one transcript whose span covers it; 'constitutive' = internal exon present in every transcript whose span covers it. first/last win over the others, then alt5/alt3, then cassette.
methods.coords: All positions are 0-based half-open on a per-gene pre-mRNA axis in transcript orientation: 0 = the 5'-most annotated base of the locus (gene.locus / gene.span give the GRCh38 span). exon.g is the exon's GRCh38 coordinate (1-based inclusive). intron.start = first intron base = donor.pos; intron.end = first base of the next exon = acceptor.pos.
methods.join: isoform.utr5_id is the tab-1 (data/utr_data.json) transcript id when the same versioned ENST is present there, else null; isoform.id equals that id whenever it exists.
methods.tss_weight: tss[i].weight is measured promoter usage, not an assumption: it is this TSS's share of the gene's FANTOM5 CAGE tags (5'-cap counts at robust CAGE peaks), averaged over a 41-library human adult tissue panel ("<tissue>, adult, poolN"), and normalised to sum to 1 over the matched TSSs of the gene. A CAGE peak is assigned to the annotated TSS it is nearest to, and only when that TSS lies within ±50 nt of the peak interval on the same strand; annotated positions converted to GRCh38 from gene.locus. Where no peak matches, weight is null (never estimated) and app/src/splice/model_exact.js renormalises over the matched promoters, or falls back to uniform mixing with a flag if a gene has none. Promoter usage is tissue-dependent: the per-promoter share across the 41 tissues is given in tss[i].weight_source.tissue and in data/tss_weights.json. Pipeline: pipeline/tss/.

exons.alias_note: the internal promoter that makes the delta133p53 variants lies in the intron immediately 3' of this exon (bourdon2005)

genes.event: The human p53 gene contains an internal promoter in intron 4 that transcribes the delta133p53 variants, whose coding sequence starts at codon 133, giving a different 5' UTR and N terminus.

splice_findings.title: deltaNp63 is the predominant p63 form in many epithelial tissues
splice_findings.evidence: Yang et al. 1998: "the predominant p63 isotypes in many epithelial tissues lack an acidic N terminus corresponding to the transactivation domain of p53". deltaNp63alpha = ENST00000354600 (MANE Plus Clinical), TAp63alpha = ENST00000264731 (MANE Select); no percentage is given in the paper.

splice_findings.title: MAPT exon 2 is included much more often than exon 3
splice_findings.evidence: Arikan et al. 2002: the two exons are alternatively spliced cassettes "in which exon 3 never appears independently of exon 2", and "exon 3 is intrinsically suboptimal and its primary regulator is a weak branch point". Consistent with VastDB compendium PSI averages 43.59 (exon 2) vs 6.20 (exon 3) (tapial2017).

splice_findings.title: MAPT exon 10 inclusion is higher from the H1 than the H2 haplotype
splice_findings.evidence: Caffrey et al. 2006, allele-specific expression in 14 H1/H2 heterozygous post-mortem control brains: exon 10+ MAPT H1:H2 transcript ratio 1.425 (SD 0.205, P < 0.0001) in globus pallidus and 1.291 (SD 0.315, P = 0.006) in frontal cortex; total MAPT did not differ. This is a haplotype contrast, not two transcript ids.

splice_findings.title: Full-length HER2 mRNA greatly exceeds the exon-16-skipped Delta16HER2 form
splice_findings.evidence: Castiglioni et al. 2006, 46 human breast carcinomas: "the DeltaHER2 splice variant represents about 9% of the HER2 mRNA" (first described by Kwong & Hung 1998, kwong1998, as an in-frame deletion of a 16-codon extracellular-domain exon). The exon-16-skipped transcript is not annotated in the Ensembl set shipped here, so 'lower' is an event label; the exon itself is E28, the 16th exon of ENST00000269571.
splice_findings.crosscheck: Independent of that paper: the ASCOT GTEx median PSI for this exon across 56 tissues is 0.96 (breast 0.97), i.e. a few percent skipping in normal tissue - the same direction as the ~9% Delta16 fraction reported in carcinomas.

splice_findings.title: Tumour cells preferentially use the internal (P2) MDM2 promoter, giving a distinct 5' UTR
splice_findings.evidence: Landers et al. 1997: in human tumour cells with stabilized wild-type p53 there is "a preferential increase in mdm2 transcription that is initiated from the internal p53-responsive promoter region of this gene", and those transcripts "contain a distinct 5' untranslated region and exhibit a significantly enhanced translational efficiency". No percentage is given; P1/P2 are not mapped to single Ensembl ids here, so both sides are event labels.
